The same object carries up to three names:

| Vocabulary | Used by | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Manuscript** | the submitted `.docx` files, and the journal | Figure S31 |
| **Repository** | this tree, and the pipeline's own output paths | `results/combined/figure_s0_roadmap.png` |
| **Deposit** | the Zenodo records, and the flat `supplementary_figures/` view | `S31_figure_s0_roadmap.png` |

The deposit name is the manuscript number, zero-padded to two digits,
followed by the output's own filename — so sorting the deposit by name
gives the order the supplement presents them in.

> **The A-numbers are not the S-numbers.** The August source document
> (`Additional_figures_080826.docx`) numbered these A1–A31, and that
> mapping was once the identity. It is not any more, and it is not even
> a permutation: one figure moved to the main text, two slots were added
> and retired, a new figure took S1, and two runs of slots rotated on
> 2026-10-19. Match a figure by its path stem, never by assuming its old
> number.

## Data S1–S4

The journal's name for the supporting data files. Note that **Data S2,
S3 and S4 are Metadata Tables M1, M2 and M3** — the repository and the
manuscript use different names for the same three tables.

| Manuscript | What it is | Repository | Where it is kept |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Data S1** | the figure-data workbook | `Data_S1_figure_data.xlsx`, built by `tools/build_data_s1.py` | Record B, as `Data_S1_figure_data.xlsx` |
| **Data S2** | Metadata Table M1 — curated per-sample metadata | `Data_S2_metadata_M1.xlsx`, built from `final_run/metadata_M1.csv` by `tools/build_data_s2.py`, which verifies every cell against it | Record A as `metadata_M1.csv`; Record B as `Data_S2_metadata_M1.xlsx` |
| **Data S3** | Metadata Table M2 — the reference catalogues | `metadata_M2.xlsx` | Record B, as `Data_S3_metadata_M2.xlsx` |
| **Data S4** | Metadata Table M3 — the VANISH/BloSSUM taxon lists | `metadata_M3.xlsx` | Record B, as `Data_S4_metadata_M3.xlsx` |

Evidence for each assignment, since no file in the pipeline derives it:

- **Data S1** — built from the stored data object behind every supplementary figure; those objects are in Record B.
- **Data S2** — badged *Data S2* on the curated-metadata and final-cohort boxes of Figure S31.
- **Data S3** — badged *Data S3* on the combined-reference box of Figure S31.
- **Data S4** — badged *Data S4* on the taxon-list box of Figure S31.

M3 describes the taxon lists the reported run derived, committed under `metadata/lists_as_analysed/`. `tools/make_submission.py` rebuilds it from `results/` after a run, and that build writes the snapshot back, so the workbook and the lists it describes cannot disagree.

## The two deposit records

**Record A** — [`10.5281/zenodo.23437518`](https://zenodo.org/records/23437518)
holds the pipeline's *inputs*: the eight per-sample breadth and depth
matrices and the curated per-sample metadata, `metadata_M1.csv`, which
is Data S2. `download_data.sh` fetches it and verifies every checksum.

**Record B** holds the pipeline's *outputs*: every submitted figure
loose and uncompressed, one file per figure under the deposit names
above, plus the result tables and the data object behind each figure,
archived per reference. `tools/build_data_s1.py` builds Data S1 from
those data objects, and the workbook it builds is deposited there too,
so Data S1 need not be rebuilt to be read.

Record B also carries all four Data S items as single files, each named
for both schemes at once — `Data_S2_metadata_M1.xlsx` and its two
siblings. The manuscript cites them as Data S2–S4; the pipeline, this
repository and Figure S31 call the same tables Metadata Tables M1–M3.
A reader who has only the deposit sees the file list before any
manifest, so the mapping has to hold in the filename itself.

Metadata Table M1 is therefore in both records: Record A carries the
`metadata_M1.csv` the pipeline reads and `download_data.sh` verifies,
and Record B carries the same table as the submitted workbook. M2 and
M3 are small enough to stay committed here as well.
